name: Bedrock
tagline: Expensify's WAN-replicated SQLite server with Paxos leader election, MySQL protocol and job/cache plugins.
description: Bedrock is a networking and distributed-transaction layer that Expensify built on SQLite and runs as the primary database behind its product. Every node holds a full SQLite copy; nodes synchronise a hashed transaction journal (marketed as a 'private blockchain'), use Paxos to elect the highest-priority node as leader, and keep accepting work across data centres and availability zones, with zero-priority 'permafollowers' adding read capacity. Clients connect with any MySQL client or driver, or Bedrock's own text protocol, and functionality comes from plugins such as DB, Jobs (a durable job queue) and Cache. Because plugins run in-process next to SQLite, custom logic avoids network round trips. The C++ codebase is LGPL-licensed and still receives near-daily commits and date-stamped releases.

scale.notes: Every node stores the full dataset; reads scale across nodes and zones while writes go through one elected leader.

strengths: Multi-datacentre replication with automatic Paxos-based failover and split-brain avoidance
Full SQLite SQL with in-process plugins that skip network serialisation
Drop-in MySQL protocol so standard clients and drivers work
Built-in durable job queue and cache plugins
Battle-tested as Expensify's production database and actively developed
weaknesses: Single-leader writes; no sharding, so the full dataset must fit every node
Small community outside Expensify and sparse operational documentation
useCases: Highly available SQL backend spanning multiple data centres
Durable job queues alongside relational data
Teams that like SQLite semantics but need replication and failover
notIdealFor: Write-heavy workloads that need horizontal write scaling
Datasets too large to replicate in full to every node
